newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Malaysia telecom firms to decide on access date.
newsitem.headline: Malaysia telecom firms to decide on access date.

text.p: Malaysian Energy, Telecommunications and Posts Minister Leo Moggie said on Thursday that telecommunications industry players will have to decide among themselves whether to have an earlier start date for equal access.
"If the industry among themselves can allow for the introduction of equal access, we have no objection," he told reporters after a telecommunications function.

Shares of national telecommunications firm Telekom Malaysia Bhd have been pressured in recent weeks on speculation that the government was willing to bring forward the scheduled start of the equal access for long-distance and international phone calls.
The equal access agreement, scheduled to start on January 1, 1999, will allow Telekom's subscribers to use networks of its rivals in making long-distance or international calls.
Moggie said the government will still abide by the 1999 start date even if the industry players are not fully ready for equal access.
Moggie also confirmed that Time Telecommunications Sdn Bhd, a subsidiary of Time Engineering Bhd "have always wanted equal access right from the start".
Analysts have said Time was pushing for the earlier start as its fixed line infrastructure is already in place, while the others are still building up theirs.
The government has awarded fixed-line licences to Time Telecommunications, Technology Resources Industries Bhd, Mutiara Telecommunications Sdn Bhd and Binariang Sdn Bhd.
